tasks.short: Detect and report equipment faults or undesirable tastes

steps.what: Observe and listen to equipment and recognise malfunctions or undesirable tastes
Report malfunctions and undesirable tastes to the supervisor with immediate context

tasks.design: Retain sensory fault detection and immediate supervisor reporting. Existing instructions in {DOCS} support escalation; no new sensor or automatically produced fault code is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Leaks, plugging, sounds and taste changes require direct observation and contextual judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: No supported software-only change removes those observations or the immediate conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising subtle changes before product or equipment is compromised.
tasks.human_edge: Sensory experience and prompt explanation of what changed.
tasks.altitude: No change to observation, reporting time or authority.

reach.task: Explain an observed equipment or taste concern for escalation
reach.learn: Local stop-work and maintenance escalation rules

evidence.claim: Retaining sensory monitoring and immediate reporting is an E1 design judgement; the digest has no equipment-fault detection case.

assumptions: Boundary is observation and reporting by the batchmaker, excluding maintenance and supervisor decisions.
The batchmaker produces the fault observation in fully retained s1 and communicates it in fully retained s2. No structured discrepancy code or digital sensor feed is assumed.
Zero upkeep because no new system or procedure is introduced.
unknowns: Current equipment safeguards and escalation procedures
research_questions: Which fault signs require immediate human escalation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=85+15=100; gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Observation and reporting remain fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor chamber temperature and adjust valves

steps.what: Observe gauges and thermometers and compare temperature with specified limits
Turn valves to control mixing chamber temperature and check the response

tasks.design: Retain gauge observation and authorised physical valve adjustment. The {OTHER} equipment controller may already regulate temperature, but its existing runtime earns no labour saving and no retrofit is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Removing observation and valve work requires validated sensing and physical control, beyond a software view.
tasks.enabler_now: No new software capability alone replaces the physical control actions described.
tasks.still_hard: Sensor reliability, thermal lag and safe response to abnormal conditions.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising an implausible reading and escalating unsafe conditions.
tasks.altitude: No change to operating time or adjustment authority.

reach.task: Escalate temperature control outside authorised limits

evidence.claim: Physical gauge monitoring and valve adjustment remain manual in this E1 design; no software-only labour saving is evidenced.

assumptions: Boundary is the batchmaker's gauge monitoring and physical adjustments, excluding controller runtime and engineering changes.

The batchmaker reads gauges in s1 with all observation time retained. Approved recipe and equipment limits are supplied by the existing authorised production process; missing or unclear limits require supervisor clarification.
No digital temperature feed, electronic setpoint or actuator is assumed. Zero upkeep because no change is introduced.
research_questions: How much human monitoring is required by current validated operating instructions?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=55+45=100; gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. No hardware or validated control change is proposed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Adjust cooking and forming operations from sampling results

steps.what: Interpret sampling results and decide permitted cooking or forming adjustments
Modify cooking and forming operations, adjusting time cycles and ingredients within authorised limits

tasks.design: Retain interpretation of samples and authorised physical process adjustment. Approved formulas may be available in {ERP}, but viewing them does not remove sensory judgement or the work of changing the process.
tasks.previous_blocker: Texture and firmness vary with actual ingredients and process conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital recipe access can support the worker without automating these decisions.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing a safe correction that achieves quality without violating process limits.
tasks.human_edge: Experience of the batch and recognition of when to stop and escalate.
tasks.altitude: No change to adjustment time or recipe-change authority.

reach.task: Clarify whether a sample result permits an in-process correction

evidence.claim: Aptean Bakery ERP stores formulas and allergen information; this supports recipe access, not automated sensory process correction.
Retaining process judgement and physical adjustments is an E1 design judgement.

assumptions: Boundary starts with sampling results and ends with an authorised adjustment; sampling and release decisions are separate tasks.

The existing sampling process produces results, and the authorised production process supplies limits. Their capture is not removed or credited as savings here; missing context requires manual clarification within retained s1.
No structured texture score, automatically calculated correction or controllable actuator is assumed. Zero upkeep because no workflow change is introduced.
research_questions: Which corrections require quality or supervisor authorisation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=50+50=100; gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Interpretation and physical adjustment remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Evaluate product samples and document sensory results

steps.what: Examine, feel and taste samples to evaluate quality, color, texture, flavor and bouquet
Document sensory results with batch and sample identification

tasks.design: Test a native quality form in {OPS_SYSTEM} that retains batch context between sample entries. The batchmaker still performs every sensory evaluation, enters its findings and verifies the saved record; only repeated metadata writing and paper handling can shrink.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper results repeat batch and sample context around each sensory observation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native quality forms can reuse verified batch context without inventing sensory findings.
tasks.still_hard: Describing subtle sensory differences and recognising an unsuitable batch.
tasks.human_edge: Taste, touch, smell and experienced quality judgement.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated record metadata; sensory decisions and release authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Agree how a sensory observation should be recorded for review

evidence.claim: Bizerba BizTrack creates food batches from traceability references and prints their identifiers; this supports batch identification capability, not sensory evaluation automation.
The native quality form and its sensory-record time estimate are E1 proposals.

assumptions: Boundary includes sensory evaluation and its record, excluding batch release, process correction and duplicate record savings elsewhere.

In s2 the batchmaker verifies or captures batch identifier, sample identifier, time, specification version and observed quality, colour, texture, flavour and bouquet. All first capture, checking and unusual free text remain within its 14 retained hours.
Existing production staff produce batch identifiers in normal batch setup; no new capture is required from them. Missing or unreadable labels require manual identification inside s2.
Test native forms before custom code. No sensory result is inferred or defaulted to passing. Savings require repeated metadata or paper handling today, not existing system runtime.
unknowns: Current recording method and duplicate metadata effort
research_questions: Does the form reduce recording time after counting all initial entry and batch checks?

already_counted.description: First capture, batch verification and sensory record checks

incremental.description: Maintain quality form fields and batch-context checks

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=80+20*0.70=94; gross=6, upkeep=1, net=5. High assumes repeated metadata and paper handling; low assumes existing single-entry recording offers no gross saving while upkeep remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Sensory monitoring and physical control stay with the batchmaker; repeated quality-record metadata may take less time.
reach: Communicate equipment concerns to production supervision
role.ambitious_version: Use small recording savings to protect attention for product and equipment observation.
